# Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal

> Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal is the first person in India to start research on 4D printing (2016). His paper "Controlled Shape Changing Components by Using 4D Printing Technology", presented at COPEN 10, IIT Madras, in 2017, is recorded as the first research in India on 4D printing. He holds a Ph.D. in four-dimensional printing from IIT Kharagpur (2024), is an Institute Postdoctoral Fellow at IIT Kanpur, and is lead editor of the Wiley book "4D Printing Technology: Principles, Materials and Applications" (2025).

Key facts:
- Name: Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal (also B. B. Samal, Bijay Bikram Samal)
- Known for: starting 4D printing research in India in 2016; first Indian research paper on 4D printing (COPEN 10, IIT Madras, 2017)
- Position: Institute Postdoctoral Fellow, Smart Materials, Structures and Systems (SMSS) Lab, Department of Mechanical Engineering, IIT Kanpur
- Education: Ph.D. (Four-Dimensional Printing), IIT Kharagpur, 2024; M.Tech (University Gold Medal), VSSUT Burla, 2018; B.Tech, BPUT (BIET Bhadrak), 2015
- Research: 4D printing, shape memory polymers, additive manufacturing, bioinspired Bouligand-auxetic metamaterials, Cargo Hyperloop
- Book: 4D Printing Technology: Principles, Materials and Applications, Wiley-Scrivener, 2025, ISBN 9781394212583, DOI 10.1002/9781394213795
- Media: Manufactur3D (2018), "Indian researchers develop the world's strongest 4D-printed parts"
- Contact: bbsamal@iitk.ac.in
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0001-5217-7041
- Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.co.in/citations?user=H_s5WZUAAAAJ

Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal
4D Printing Institute Postdoctoral Fellow IIT Kanpur Wiley Book Editor
Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal is an Institute Postdoctoral Fellow in the Smart Materials, Structures & Systems Lab, Department of Mechanical Engineering, IIT Kanpur , where he works with Prof. Bishakh Bhattacharya. He is interested in materials that change their shape over time, known as 4D printing , and in the structures and machines that can be built from them.
He began working on 4D printing in 2016 as an M.Tech student at VSSUT Burla. His 2017 paper at COPEN 10, IIT Madras, is recorded as the first research on 4D printing in India . He went on to complete a Ph.D. on four-dimensional printing at IIT Kharagpur under Prof. C. S. Kumar and Prof. S. K. Varshney, and to edit the Wiley book 4D Printing Technology with them. At IIT Kanpur he works on bioinspired Bouligand-auxetic metamaterials and the Cargo Hyperloop project, and enjoys teaching and mentoring students along the way.

Research Journey
The work has grown one step at a time: a low-cost FDM printer built as a B.Tech project in 2015, shape-changing parts in 2016, a Ph.D. on 4D printing at IIT Kharagpur, a Wiley book with his mentors, and now metamaterials and transport systems at IIT Kanpur, always with the guidance of mentors and the help of many collaborators and students.

Research
Dr. Samal's research covers 4D printing, shape memory polymers, bioinspired metamaterials, sustainable polymers and laser post-processing of metal additive manufacturing. His work appears in journals such as Smart Materials and Structures , Science of the Total Environment , Thin-Walled Structures and Sensors and Actuators A , and in books from Wiley, Elsevier and CRC Press .
He has presented at international conferences in Germany, the USA, the Netherlands and South Korea , including a Highlight Lecture at MSE 2024, Darmstadt. He mentors two Ph.D. scholars and has guided six research interns and two B.Tech projects.

4D Printing in India
How 4D printing research began in India in 2016, and who started it.
2016 4D printing research begins in India
2017 India's first 4D printing paper (COPEN 10, IIT Madras)
2018 "World's strongest 4D-printed parts" (Manufactur3D)
2025 Wiley book: 4D Printing Technology
Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal started 4D printing research in India in 2016. His paper "Controlled Shape Changing Components by Using 4D Printing Technology", presented at the 10th International Conference on Precision, Meso, Micro and Nano Engineering (COPEN 10) at IIT Madras in 2017, is recorded as the first research in India on 4D printing.
What is 4D printing?
4D printing is 3D printing of smart materials that change shape over time . A part is printed from a stimulus-responsive material, usually a shape memory polymer, then "programmed" by heating, deforming and cooling it. Later, when the part meets a trigger such as heat, water or light, it moves into a new shape on its own. Time is the fourth dimension.
Because the shape change is built into the material, 4D printing can make self-folding structures, grippers and actuators without motors, deployable medical devices and adaptive metamaterials.
How 4D printing research started in India
In 2016 , as an M.Tech student in Manufacturing Systems Engineering at Veer Surendra Sai University of Technology (VSSUT), Burla , Bijaya Bikram Samal began printing shape memory polymers on fused deposition modelling (FDM) printers and programming them to change shape in a controlled way. A year earlier, as a B.Tech student, he had built an FDM 3D printer from scratch.
In 2017 he presented this work with A. Jena and D. Mishra at COPEN 10, IIT Madras : Controlled Shape Changing Components by Using 4D Printing Technology . It is recorded as the first research in India on 4D printing .
In 2018 , the international magazine Manufactur3D reported that Indian researchers had developed the world's strongest 4D-printed parts . The same year his M.Tech thesis, Controlled Shape Changing Components using 4D Printing , earned the University Gold Medal.
A Ph.D. dedicated to 4D printing
From 2018 he pursued a Ph.D. on the subject at IIT Kharagpur with an MHRD Doctoral Fellowship. His thesis, Four-Dimensional Printing: Shape Programming, Material Characterization, and Parametric Optimization , was awarded on 30 December 2024. Papers from this work appear in Smart Materials and Structures , the Journal of Mechanical Science and Technology and Materials Today: Proceedings , and he presented it in Germany, the USA, South Korea and the Netherlands.
A book on 4D printing
In 2025 Wiley-Scrivener published 4D Printing Technology: Principles, Materials and Application , with Dr. Samal as lead editor and author of six chapters, from the history of 3D-to-4D printing to characterization techniques and photonics applications.
4D printing research today
At IIT Kanpur , Dr. Samal now works on 4D-printed bioinspired Bouligand-auxetic metamaterials , multi-material direct ink writing, and a 4D-printed mechanical steganography device developed in consultation with the Indian Army. He also teaches 3D/4D printing workshops across India, from NIT Tiruchirappalli to NERIST in Arunachal Pradesh.

Frequently Asked Questions
Who started 4D printing research in India?
Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal started 4D printing research in India in 2016, as an M.Tech student at Veer Surendra Sai University of Technology, Burla. His paper "Controlled Shape Changing Components by Using 4D Printing Technology", presented at COPEN 10, IIT Madras, in 2017, is recorded as the first research in India on 4D printing.
What is 4D printing?
4D printing is 3D printing of smart materials, such as shape memory polymers, that are programmed to change shape, stiffness or function over time when exposed to a stimulus like heat, water or light. Time is the fourth dimension.
Where is 4D printing research done in India?
Dr. Samal's 4D printing work began at VSSUT Burla (2016–2018), continued through his Ph.D. on four-dimensional printing at IIT Kharagpur (awarded 2024), and now continues at IIT Kanpur, where he works on 4D-printed bioinspired Bouligand-auxetic metamaterials.
Is there a book on 4D printing by an Indian author?
Yes. Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal is the lead editor of "4D Printing Technology: Principles, Materials and Application" (Wiley-Scrivener, 2025), part of the Advances in Additive Manufacturing series.
What are the applications of 4D printing?
Applications include self-folding and deployable structures, soft robotic actuators, biomedical devices, photonics, smart textiles, and adaptive metamaterials that absorb impact or isolate vibration.


==== https://www.drbijay.com/what-is-4d-printing.html ====
What is 4D Printing?
A plain-language guide by Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal, who has worked on 4D printing since 2016.
3D + time A printed part that changes shape later
SMPs Shape memory polymers are the most common material
Stimulus Heat, water, light, magnetic or electric field
2016 4D printing research begins in India
4D printing is the 3D printing of stimulus-responsive ("smart") materials so that the printed object changes its shape, properties or function over time when it is exposed to a stimulus such as heat, water, light, a magnetic field or an electric field. The fourth dimension is time.
4D printing in one minute
In ordinary 3D printing, a part keeps the shape it was printed in. In 4D printing, the part is designed to move after printing: a flat sheet folds itself into a box, a lattice shrinks to absorb an impact, a gripper closes when it is warmed. The motion is not driven by motors. It is stored in the material and in the way the part was printed and programmed.
How does 4D printing work?
Every 4D-printed part needs three things:
A smart material that responds to a stimulus, for example a shape memory polymer (SMP), a shape memory alloy such as nickel–titanium (NiTi), a hydrogel or a liquid crystal elastomer.
A design that turns the material's response into a useful motion, such as a hinge, a bilayer, an auxetic lattice or a gradient of layers.
A stimulus that triggers the change: hot water or air, moisture, UV or visible light, a magnetic field or an electric current.
For shape memory polymers, the part is usually programmed after printing. It is heated above its transition temperature, deformed into a temporary shape, and cooled so that the shape is fixed. When it is heated again, it returns to the printed shape. How well it does this is measured by the shape fixity ratio and the shape recovery ratio .
Programming strategies
The same printed part can behave very differently depending on how it is programmed. Dr. Samal's work compares programming above and below the glass transition temperature (hot and cold programming) and shows how the choice changes recovery, stiffness and the material's internal structure ( Smart Materials and Structures, 2023 ). His later work shows that infill density, bed temperature and build orientation in fused deposition modelling (FDM) also change the shape memory behaviour ( J. Mech. Sci. Technol., 2024 ).
Which 3D printing processes are used?
Fused deposition modelling (FDM / FFF): low-cost printing of thermoplastic SMPs such as PLA and TPU. Printing itself can pre-strain the material.
Direct ink writing (DIW): extrusion of hydrogels, elastomers and composite inks, often with several materials.
Vat photopolymerisation (SLA, DLP) and PolyJet: fine features and multi-material parts.
Two-photon polymerisation: micro- and nanoscale 4D printing.
Laser powder bed fusion (LPBF) and directed energy deposition: shape memory alloys such as NiTi.
Applications of 4D printing
Self-folding and deployable structures for space, packaging and architecture
Soft robotic grippers and actuators that need no motors
Biomedical devices such as stents, scaffolds and implants that change shape in the body
Mechanical metamaterials that absorb impact or isolate vibration, including auxetic and bioinspired Bouligand designs
Photonics, sensors and smart textiles
Security devices: Dr. Samal's lab has built a 4D-printed mechanical steganography device that hides and reveals information
4D printing vs 3D printing
Feature 3D printing 4D printing
Shape after printing Fixed Changes over time
Materials Any printable material Stimulus-responsive (smart) materials
Extra step Post-processing Programming and a trigger
Typical use Prototypes, tooling, end-use parts Actuators, deployable and adaptive structures
A short history
The term "4D printing" was introduced by Skylar Tibbits at MIT in 2013. Research then grew quickly worldwide. In India , 4D printing research began in 2016 , when Bijaya Bikram Samal started work on controlled shape-changing components at VSSUT Burla. His 2017 paper at COPEN 10, IIT Madras, is recorded as the first research on 4D printing in India. Read the full history of 4D printing in India .
Further reading
For a full treatment, see 4D Printing Technology: Principles, Materials and Applications (Wiley-Scrivener, 2025), edited by B. B. Samal, C. S. Kumar and S. K. Varshney, and the list of 4D printing publications .
Key terms
Shape memory polymer (SMP) A polymer that remembers its printed shape and returns to it when heated
Glass transition temperature (T g ) The temperature above which an SMP becomes soft and can be reshaped
Shape fixity / recovery ratio How well a temporary shape is held, and how fully the original shape returns
Metamaterial A structure whose properties come from its geometry, such as a lattice that shrinks sideways when compressed
4D Printing FAQ
What is 4D printing in simple words?
4D printing is 3D printing with smart materials, so the printed object can change its shape or properties later on its own when it is heated, wetted, lit or exposed to a magnetic or electric field. Time is the fourth dimension.
What materials are used in 4D printing?
The most common are shape memory polymers (for example PLA- and polyurethane-based materials), shape memory alloys such as NiTi, hydrogels, liquid crystal elastomers, and composites with magnetic or conductive fillers.
Who started 4D printing research in India?
Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal started 4D printing research in India in 2016. His paper "Controlled Shape Changing Components by Using 4D Printing Technology", presented at COPEN 10, IIT Madras, in 2017, is recorded as the first research in India on 4D printing.
What is the difference between 3D printing and 4D printing?
A 3D-printed part keeps the shape it was printed in. A 4D-printed part is made from a stimulus-responsive material and is designed to change its shape, stiffness or function over time.
Is there a textbook on 4D printing?
Yes. 4D Printing Technology: Principles, Materials and Applications (Wiley-Scrivener, 2025), edited by Bijaya Bikram Samal, Cheruvu Siva Kumar and Shailendra Kumar Varshney, covers principles, materials, characterization and applications.

About Dr. Samal
From building a 3D printer as a B.Tech student to starting 4D printing research in India.
Dr. Bijaya Bikram Samal
Dr. Samal grew up in Bhadrak, Odisha, and studied mechanical engineering at BIET Bhadrak, where he led the team that built a low-cost FDM 3D printer as their final-year project. That project grew into a question he has followed ever since: what if a printed part could change its shape on its own?
He started working on 4D printing in 2016 during his M.Tech at VSSUT Burla, and his 2017 COPEN 10 paper at IIT Madras is recorded as the first research on 4D printing in India. After a Ph.D. on the subject at IIT Kharagpur, he joined IIT Kanpur , where he is now an Institute Postdoctoral Fellow in Prof. Bishakh Bhattacharya's Smart Materials, Structures & Systems Lab, working on bioinspired metamaterials and as Team Leader of the Cargo Hyperloop project.
He is grateful to his teachers, mentors, colleagues, students and family, whose support made each step possible.

The Journey
A decade in additive manufacturing, told in milestones.
2015 Built a 3D printer from scratch
B.Tech in Mechanical Engineering (BPUT, BIET Bhadrak). Led the design, assembly and testing of a low-cost FDM 3D printer as his capstone project.
2016 Started 4D printing research in India
As an M.Tech student at VSSUT Burla, began programming 3D-printed shape memory polymers into shape-changing components.
2017 First paper on 4D printing in India
"Controlled Shape Changing Components by Using 4D Printing Technology", COPEN 10, IIT Madras.
2018 University Gold Medal
M.Tech with CGPA 9.88. The 4D-printed parts were featured by Manufactur3D, and the work received the Chief Minister Award & Startup Grant.
2018–23 Ph.D. at IIT Kharagpur
MHRD Doctoral Fellowship for a Ph.D. dedicated to four-dimensional printing; Best Research Paper Award (FRESM, 2021).
2023 On the international stage
Talks in Frankfurt, Atlanta and Songdo; Chartered Engineer (India); IOP Trusted Reviewer.
2024 Ph.D. awarded · Highlight Lecture
Ph.D. conferred on 30 Dec 2024. Highlight Lecture and symposium organizer at MSE 2024, Darmstadt. Fellow, Bose Science Society.
2025 Wiley book and IIT Kanpur
Lead editor of 4D Printing Technology (Wiley). Joined IIT Kanpur; Team Leader, Cargo Hyperloop; Institute Postdoctoral Fellow from November.
2026 Fellowship, patents and teaching
JST Sakura Science Fellowship (Japan), two Indian patents filed, four Q1-level papers, and tutor for TA111 at IIT Kanpur.

==== https://www.drbijay.com/research.html ====
Research Areas
Smart materials that move, structures that adapt, and the machines that make them.
Research Interests
Research at the Smart Materials, Structures & Systems Lab, IIT Kanpur , building on a decade of work in additive manufacturing that began with India's first 4D printing research in 2016 .
Core
4D printing of shape memory polymers
Programming strategies, infill and temperature effects, build orientation, and shape fixity and recovery of FDM-printed SMPs.
Papers
Current
Bioinspired metamaterials
4D-printed Bouligand-auxetic metastructures with orientation-dependent stiffness, energy absorption and wave isolation.
Patent
Process
Multi-material additive manufacturing
Freeform and direct ink writing of soft materials and biomaterials with in-situ mixing, heating and cooling.
Technology
Applications
Soft robotic actuators & hydrogels
Functional hydrogels and SMA/SMP actuators, including Nitinol actuators with bead-on-fiber coatings.
Papers
Metals
Laser post-processing of metal AM
Laser polishing and surface modification of laser powder bed fusion parts, such as cobalt-chrome alloys.
Papers
Sustainability
Biodegradable polymers for AM
Printability, dimensional accuracy and anaerobic biodegradability of PHA and PHB filaments and printed parts.
Papers
Key Findings
What the published work shows, in brief. Each links to the paper.
Programming decides how a 4D-printed part behaves
Comparing two thermo-mechanical programming methods on FDM-printed shape memory polymer showed clear differences in shape fixity, recovery and material properties, supported by thermal and structural characterization. Smart Materials and Structures, 2023
Print settings are part of the "program"
Infill density and bed temperature in FDM change the shape memory response under different programming conditions, so they can be tuned to control how a part recovers. Work on build orientation is under review. J. Mech. Sci. Technol., 2024
Lattices that shrink when heated
Thermo-mechanically programmed honeycomb and negative-honeycomb (auxetic) structures can be made to expand or to compress on heating; heat-induced compression was demonstrated using the group's programming process (Highlight Lecture, MSE 2024, Darmstadt). Conference record
Truly biodegradable 3D printing
Unlike PLA, which does not break down under typical landfill or anaerobic digestion conditions, PHB filament and its 3D-printed sheets were shown to biodegrade anaerobically using the biochemical methane potential test. Science of the Total Environment, 2025
Smoother metal AM parts with laser polishing
A design-of-experiments approach identified laser polishing settings that reduce the surface roughness of cobalt-chrome parts made by laser powder bed fusion. Int. J. Adv. Manuf. Technol., 2024
3D-printed metasurfaces that block vibration
Peridynamics modelling and experiments show how 3D-printed shells and mechanical metasurfaces isolate elastic waves. Thin-Walled Structures, 2026

Technologies & Patents
Working prototypes and filed Indian patents from the lab.
Technologies Developed
Each has reached Technology Readiness Level 4: validated in the laboratory.
Low-cost shape-memory characterization system
Measures shape fixity and recovery of 4D-printed parts. Benchmarked against commercial systems and used in laboratory studies behind his publications.
TRL 4 of 9 Lab validated
4D-printed mechanical steganography & encryption–decryption device
A laboratory prototype developed in consultation with the Indian Army that hides and reveals information through programmed shape change. Under laboratory testing.
TRL 4 of 9 Under testing
Cargo Hyperloop demonstrator
A fully functional 1:20-scale prototype integrating the core functions of the proposed compressed-air cargo transport system, for CMPDI, Ministry of Coal. Watch the film
TRL 4 of 9 Working demonstrator
Multi-material direct ink writing (DIW) 3D printer
Prints soft materials and biomaterials with in-situ material mixing, heating and cooling. Under laboratory testing.
TRL 4 of 9 Under testing
